[guideline: BURNS AND SCALDS p29] Cool the burn under running water for 20 minutes. Estimate the area burned. Burns over 10% of the body, burns of the face, hands, feet, genitals or airway, and all electrical burns must be referred. Give paracetamol, cover with a clean dressing, give tetanus toxoid if not immunised.
2 year old spilled hot tea on the forearm, about the size of the child's palm, blistered. Crying but ok.

ACTION: ADVISE
STM: BURNS AND SCALDS
---
Cool under running water for 20 minutes.
Small burn, not face or hands: cover with a clean dressing, paracetamol for pain.
Check tetanus immunisation.
Review in 2 days; refer if the burn gets infected or is larger than you thought.

[guideline: ASTHMA p23] Mild wheeze: salbutamol 2-6 puffs through a spacer, repeat every 20 minutes up to 3 times. Severe asthma (cannot talk, chest indrawing, cyanosis, drowsy): continuous salbutamol, oxygen, prednisolone 1 mg/kg and refer urgently. First wheeze under 1 year: think bronchiolitis or pneumonia.
5 year old wheezing, cannot speak in sentences, chest indrawing, lips going blue. No transport today.

ACTION: REFER_NOW
STM: ASTHMA
---
Severe asthma with cyanosis: this child must be referred now; radio for transport.
Give salbutamol 6 puffs through a spacer, repeat every 20 minutes without stopping.
Oxygen if available, prednisolone 1 mg/kg by mouth.
Do not leave the child alone; sit upright.

[guideline: MALARIA p53] All children with fever should have a malaria test (RDT or blood slide). Uncomplicated malaria: artemether-lumefantrine by weight twice daily for 3 days with food: 5-14 kg 1 tablet per dose, 15-24 kg 2 tablets, 25-34 kg 3 tablets. Severe malaria (unable to drink, convulsions, lethargy, severe anaemia, jaundice): give artesunate IM or rectal and refer urgently. If no test is available and fever has no other cause, treat as malaria and refer for testing.
Visit note: boy, 3 years, 13 kg, fever 2 days, not eating much, RDT positive falciparum, drinking ok, no danger signs. Gave Coartem 1 tab bd 3 days and paracetamol 195 mg. Review 2 days.

ACTION: ADVISE
STM: MALARIA

[guideline: DIARRHOEA p38] Assess dehydration. No dehydration: ORS after each loose stool (50-100 ml under 2 years, 100-200 ml over 2 years), continue feeding, zinc 10 mg daily under 6 months or 20 mg daily from 6 months for 10 days. Some dehydration: ORS 75 ml/kg over 4 hours at the clinic then reassess. Severe dehydration (lethargic, sunken eyes, drinks poorly, skin pinch goes back very slowly): IV fluids and refer urgently.
18 month old, 10 kg, diarrhoea 2 days. Eyes a bit sunken, drinks eagerly, skin pinch slow. Not lethargic.

ACTION: ADVISE
STM: DIARRHOEA
---
Some dehydration. Give ORS 75 ml/kg = 750 ml over 4 hours at the clinic, small sips often.
Reassess after 4 hours; if better continue ORS at home after each stool.
Zinc 20 mg daily for 10 days, keep feeding.
If the child becomes lethargic or cannot drink, send on the next boat with ORS on the way.

Severe pneumonia (chest indrawing, danger signs, oxygen saturation under 90%): give the first dose of antibiotic, oxygen if available, and refer urgently.

Sapos chest indrawing, hem no save drink, o slip tumas: sendem long nekis bot.
